When execution is costly, a privacy layer that wants to rule out sandwiches profitable at every consistent size may therefore reveal anything about the size except a lower bound above an explicit threshold; the upper end of the range is irrelevant. With two or more symmetric traders, every pure-strategy perfect Bayesian equilibrium of the auction hands the entire expected net rent to the auctioneer. If the direction is hidden too, no non-contingent first leg front-runs both possible directions, while post-trade arbitrage can survive even perfect pre-trade hiding.
tldr: The paper derives exact leakage thresholds for private mempools in constant-product AMMs, showing how much information about a victim's trade size can be revealed before sandwich attacks become profitable.
motivation: Private and encrypted mempools aim to prevent MEV extraction such as sandwich attacks, but they often leak partial information about pending transactions, raising the question of how much leakage is tolerable.
method: The authors model a fee-free constant-product AMM where traders observe an interval for the victim's size and bid in a first-price auction for the right to front-run, under an executability constraint across all consistent sizes.
result: The smallest size consistent with the leak determines feasible front-runs, the largest such front-run is optimal for pointwise, expected, and worst-case profit, and guaranteed profit has a closed form; with symmetric competition, all expected net rent goes to the auctioneer.
conclusion: A privacy layer can rule out profitable sandwiches by revealing anything except a lower bound above an explicit threshold, while hiding direction prevents non-contingent first-leg front-running but does not eliminate post-trade arbitrage.

title: Multidimensional Political Attitudes And Polarization Across 141 Countries
authors: Hazem Ibrahim, Aymane Omari, Aaron R. Kaufman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Societies worldwide are described as increasingly polarized, yet issue polarization -- how divided a society is over political positions -- has been measured almost entirely on a single left-right axis developed in Western democracies. Whether that axis describes political division elsewhere is largely untested, because no survey measures political attitudes on multiple dimensions across many countries. Here, we harmonize 1,299 items from nine cross-national survey programs and 23 national election studies to place 1.14 million people from 141 countries on four dimensions: social liberalism, economic left-right, democratic commitment, and anti-elite sentiment. A single left-right axis does not describe political division in most of the world. The median within-country correlation between a person's social and economic positions is -0.015. Societies differ instead in what they are divided about, and they do so by region. European countries divide most often over social liberalism, East Asian and Arab countries over democratic commitment, Latin American countries over economic left-right, and African countries over anti-elite sentiment. Of the 81 countries measured on all four dimensions, 39 are most divided on a dimension no left-right scale would capture. Most political disagreement lies within countries rather than between them, at 58 to 88 percent of the variance. Ideological constraint, long treated as a property of mass publics, holds in nineteen of the eighty-three we can test, most strongly in the United States at +0.70, and there it is concentrated among the politically attentive. Understanding political conflict therefore requires asking not how polarized a society is but what it is polarized about. Our released item bank and fitted parameters place respondents from any future survey on the same scale without re-estimation, once that survey's items are harmonized to the bank.
tldr: A large-scale harmonization of 1,299 survey items across 141 countries shows that political division is multidimensional and that a single left-right axis fails to capture polarization in most of the world.
motivation: Political polarization is typically measured on a single Western-derived left-right axis, but whether that axis describes political division outside Western democracies has been largely untested due to a lack of multi-dimensional cross-national survey data.
method: The authors harmonized 1,299 items from nine cross-national survey programs and 23 national election studies to place 1.14 million respondents from 141 countries on four dimensions: social liberalism, economic left-right, democratic commitment, and anti-elite sentiment.
result: The median within-country correlation between social and economic positions is only -0.015, and societies differ by region in what they are divided about; 39 of 81 fully measured countries are most divided on a dimension no left-right scale would capture, with 58-88% of disagreement variance lying within countries.
conclusion: Understanding political conflict requires asking what a society is polarized about rather than how polarized it is, and the released item bank allows future surveys to be placed on the same scale without re-estimation.

title: Loop Content Of Bond Percolation On Hyperbolic Triangulations: An Exact Identity And A $1/\lambda$ Expansion
authors: Zachary Treisman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the homology of percolation clusters on disk-shaped patches of the regular [MATH] triangle tilings for [MATH]. Varying [MATH] gives a one-parameter family of hyperbolic tilings, from mildly curved ([MATH]) to deeply hyperbolic ([MATH]), and this paper measures and derives loop content as a function of curvature. A single growth-rate parameter [MATH], the asymptotic ratio of successive ring sizes, governs every result. Total persistent [MATH] of the bond-percolation complex, per vertex, is measured across [MATH] and found to be a nearly linear function of [MATH]. An exact identity reduces total loop persistence to the weight of the lattice's minimum spanning tree minus a boundary correction. The boundary correction follows from the ring recursion, and the spanning-tree weight is derived to first order in [MATH] by attaching rings one at a time to a contracted interior, with a correction for loops that close through the ring outside. The resulting formula has no free parameters, gives the large-curvature intercept in closed form as [MATH], and agrees with the measurements to within the size of the next-order term.
tldr: The paper studies loop homology in bond-percolation clusters on hyperbolic triangle tilings, deriving an exact identity and a 1/lambda expansion relating loop persistence to minimum spanning tree weight and boundary corrections.
motivation: Understanding how curvature affects percolation cluster topology may provide insight into hyperbolic lattices and statistical mechanics on negatively curved spaces.
method: The authors measure persistent homology of bond-percolation complexes on disk-shaped patches of regular hyperbolic triangulations and derive an exact identity plus an expansion in the growth-rate parameter lambda.
result: Total loop persistence per vertex scales nearly linearly with curvature, and an exact identity reduces it to the minimum spanning tree weight minus a boundary correction, with a parameter-free formula matching measurements to next order.
conclusion: The work provides an analytic handle on loop content in hyperbolic percolation, but its focus on geometric percolation and homology is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Formalization Of Langlands's Second Main Lemma For Local Epsilon Factors
authors: Fukuhiro Ueda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize in Lean 4 Langlands's Second Main Lemma for local epsilon factors over nonarchimedean local fields. The lemma compares local constants of characters of distinct intermediate fields in a bicyclic Galois extension. The proof follows the author's companion mathematical paper and uses the formalization of the First Main Lemma. The First Main Lemma gives only a power relation, leaving a root-of-unity ambiguity. Resolving this ambiguity is the main part of the proof and requires further analysis according to ramification. The wild dyadic case is the mathematically new part of the companion proof, and its Lean formalization provides a machine-checked verification of this new case. Both mixed and equal characteristic are included. We give the exact Lean statement, identify the declarations used in the individual cases, and describe six simplifications of the mathematical proof suggested by the formalization. ChatGPT assisted with transferring formulas and citations from the mathematical manuscript and with adding references to the corresponding Lean source, and suggested improvements to the wording of the paper.
tldr: This paper formalizes Langlands's Second Main Lemma for local epsilon factors over nonarchimedean local fields in Lean 4.
motivation: The goal is to provide a machine-checked verification of a key lemma in the Langlands program, particularly the new wild dyadic case, and to identify simplifications in the mathematical proof.
method: The formalization uses Lean 4 and builds on the formalization of the First Main Lemma, resolving a root-of-unity ambiguity through ramification analysis.
result: The paper gives the exact Lean statement, identifies declarations used in individual cases, and describes six simplifications of the mathematical proof suggested by the formalization.
conclusion: This work contributes to the formal verification of advanced number theory and the Langlands program, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Freezing Calder\'on: Robust Preconditioning For Maxwell Scattering Under Shape Uncertainty
authors: Carlos Jerez-Hanckes Paul Escapil-Inchausp\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Calder\'on preconditioning restores mesh-independent conditioning for boundary-element discretizations of the Maxwell electric field integral equation, but assembling the dual barycentric operator can dominate the computational cost. We show that this preconditioner can be assembled once at a nominal geometry and reused across connectivity-preserving shape perturbations. Exact combinatorial alignment of the RWG-BC degrees of freedom transports the duality pairing, leaving only the dual-mesh operator frozen. Under uniform discrete-stability and geometric operator-continuity assumptions, a bi-parametric operator-preconditioning analysis yields a spectral-condition-number bound uniform in the mesh size and, after tensorization, in the stochastic-Galerkin dimension. Numerical experiments on smooth and non-smooth scatterers show that the frozen preconditioner closely tracks freshly assembled Calder\'on preconditioners over substantial shape variations. A Monte Carlo campaign on a NASA almond, whose admissibility is screened before each shape is constructed so that no realization is rejected, separates the two strategies by less than the variation between realizations, and mesh refinement there leaves the frozen iteration count unchanged. Reuse yields roughly 30x measured speedup per new realization in our dense implementation; a cost-model estimate based on published compressed-assembly timings gives roughly 2x.
tldr: The paper proposes freezing Calderón preconditioners assembled at a nominal geometry for reuse across connectivity-preserving shape perturbations in Maxwell scattering, with uniform condition-number bounds and numerical speedups.
motivation: Calderón preconditioning improves conditioning for Maxwell boundary-element discretizations, but assembling the dual barycentric operator can dominate computational cost, especially when many shape realizations are needed.
method: Exact combinatorial alignment of RWG-BC degrees of freedom transports the duality pairing, and a bi-parametric operator-preconditioning analysis under uniform discrete-stability and geometric continuity assumptions yields spectral-condition-number bounds.
result: Numerical experiments on smooth and non-smooth scatterers and a NASA almond Monte Carlo campaign show the frozen preconditioner tracks freshly assembled ones, with roughly 30x measured speedup per new realization in dense implementation (estimated 2x for compressed assembly).
conclusion: Reusing a nominal-geometry Calderón preconditioner is robust under shape uncertainty and maintains mesh-independent iteration counts, offering a practical acceleration for stochastic Maxwell scattering problems.

title: On Standard Perturbations Of The Affine Twist Map
authors: Salvador Addas Zanata
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any [MATH], consider the Affine twist map [MATH] given by $[MATH][MATH][MATH]t[MATH]t[MATH][MATH]\{t\}.[MATH]k\in,[MATH][MATH][MATH]t=p/q[MATH]p[MATH]q>0[MATH]k_{p/q}>0[MATH]|k|<k_{p/q}[MATH]f_{k,p/q}[MATH]\{p/q\}.[MATH]t[MATH]k\neq 0[MATH]f_{k,t}[MATH]t[MATH]f_{k,t}[MATH]k$.
tldr: The paper studies standard perturbations of the affine twist map, a purely dynamical-systems problem with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The affine twist map is a fundamental model in Hamiltonian dynamics, and the author aims to understand how its dynamics change under standard perturbations.
method: The analysis appears to establish parameter thresholds k_{p/q} and proves existence or nonexistence of invariant curves or orbits for perturbations f_{k,p/q} depending on rotation number p/q.
result: For sufficiently small perturbations |k| < k_{p/q}, the perturbed map f_{k,p/q} exhibits dynamical behavior associated with the rotation number p/q, while for k ≠ 0 certain properties of the unperturbed map are altered.
conclusion: The work contributes to the classical theory of twist maps and perturbative Hamiltonian dynamics, but it falls entirely outside the listed quantum-information-related research directions.

title: Tr-ssqp: A Trust-Region Method For Constrained Stochastic Optimization Under Heavy-Tailed Noise
authors: Haoxuan Wang, Yuchen Fang, Sen Na
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider stochastic nonlinear optimization problems with deterministic equality constraints. While unconstrained stochastic optimization is well understood, the interplay between optimality and feasibility in the constrained setting poses significant challenges. Moreover, existing theoretical guarantees for constrained stochastic methods predominantly rely on bounded-variance assumptions, leaving the heavy-tailed noise regime largely unexplored. To address this gap, we propose a novel trust-region method within the stochastic sequential quadratic programming framework, termed TR-SSQP. Our method employs a normal-tangential decomposition in the step computation to balance optimality and feasibility. In addition, we incorporate a normalization mechanism in the design of the trust-region radius, together with Polyak momentum for gradient estimation, ensuring stable updates without gradient clipping. When the trust-region radius and the momentum parameter decay at appropriate rates, we establish global almost-sure convergence of the method. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first asymptotic convergence result for constrained stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed noise. We demonstrate the promising performance of the proposed method through extensive numerical experiments, including comparisons among its variants and with existing constrained stochastic optimization methods.
tldr: The paper introduces TR-SSQP, a trust-region stochastic sequential quadratic programming method for constrained stochastic optimization that achieves global almost-sure convergence under heavy-tailed gradient noise.
motivation: Existing theoretical guarantees for constrained stochastic optimization rely on bounded-variance assumptions, leaving the heavy-tailed noise regime largely unexplored despite its practical importance.
method: The method uses a normal-tangential decomposition for step computation to balance optimality and feasibility, a normalized trust-region radius, and Polyak momentum for gradient estimation, avoiding gradient clipping.
result: With appropriate decay rates for the trust-region radius and momentum parameter, the authors establish global almost-sure convergence, claimed as the first asymptotic convergence result for constrained stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed noise, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: TR-SSQP provides a theoretically grounded and empirically effective approach for constrained stochastic optimization in heavy-tailed noise settings.

title: Optimal Prophet Inequalities For Gain From Trade
authors: Xujin Chen, Xiaodong Hu, Changjun Wang, Qingjie Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We initiate the study of prophet trading, an online trading model in which a trader interacts with sellers and buyers who arrive in a uniformly random order and whose prices are drawn independently from a common known distribution. The trader aims to maximize the expected gain from trade (GFT), with performance measured against an omniscient prophet that knows the realized arrival order and all prices in advance. Unlike the classical prophet inequality problem, the trader must make both purchasing and selling decisions while managing the inventory, which makes both the prophet benchmark and the analysis of online algorithms substantially more intricate. For arbitrary numbers of buyers and sellers, we propose a simple threshold-based algorithm and prove a distribution-free competitive ratio of~2, which is the best possible. Our main technical contribution is an exact characterization of the inventory process induced by threshold trading. By expressing the algorithm's expected GFT in terms of the cumulative holding probability at buyer arrivals, we derive an exact formula for this inventory term, which serves as the foundation of our analysis and yields sharper guarantees in several important special cases. For balanced trading (with [MATH] sellers and [MATH] buyers), we improve the competitive ratio to [MATH], which is strictly less than 2 for every [MATH]. For the single-seller case, we sharpen the analysis of the fixed-threshold algorithm to obtain an asymptotic competitive ratio of [MATH]. Furthermore, by exploiting the additional structure of this setting, we design an adaptive-threshold algorithm whose competitive ratio approaches [MATH]. Due to a symmetry property of our general algorithmic idea, the same [MATH]-competitive guarantee also holds for the single-buyer case.
tldr: The paper studies prophet trading, an online model for maximizing expected gain from trade when buyers and sellers arrive in random order with prices from a known distribution.
motivation: Classical prophet inequalities are extended to a trading setting where the decision-maker must both buy and sell while managing inventory, making the prophet benchmark and online algorithm analysis more complex.
method: The authors propose a simple threshold-based algorithm, derive an exact characterization of the induced inventory process, and design adaptive-threshold algorithms for special cases like single-seller and single-buyer.
result: They prove a distribution-free competitive ratio of 2 for arbitrary numbers of buyers and sellers, improve it to below 2 for balanced trading, and obtain sharper asymptotic ratios for single-seller and single-buyer cases.
conclusion: The work establishes tight or improved prophet inequalities for gain from trade, advancing the theory of online trading with inventory constraints.

title: Rough Spectral Asymptotics For Commutators Of General Singular Integrals
authors: Tuomas Hyt\"onen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Schatten class membership of commutators arising from Connes' quantised calculus has been characterised in a general framework, which covers multiple concrete situations of interest. In contrast to this, related results dealing with the asymptotic behaviour of the singular values of these commutators have been restricted to a relatively short list of specific examples only. In this work, we show that a version of the spectral asymptotic formula, involving comparable lower and upper limits in place of an exact limit, remains valid in great generality of singular integrals over metric measure spaces. A key proof ingredient of independent interest is a new asymptotic version of the Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem. We also present a new approach to commutator upper bounds at the critical index; while not quite as general as more elaborate methods, it is general enough to reproduce the known upper bounds in Heisenberg and Carnot groups in a much simpler way.
tldr: This paper establishes rough spectral asymptotic formulas for singular values of commutators of general singular integrals over metric measure spaces, extending known Schatten-class results.
motivation: Prior work characterized Schatten class membership of commutators from Connes' quantised calculus, but spectral asymptotics were known only for a short list of specific examples.
method: The author proves a general rough spectral asymptotic formula using comparable lower and upper limits instead of exact limits, with a new asymptotic Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem as a key ingredient and a simpler approach to upper bounds at the critical index.
result: The spectral asymptotic formula is shown to hold in great generality for singular integrals on metric measure spaces, reproducing known upper bounds for Heisenberg and Carnot groups more simply.
conclusion: The work advances the mathematical theory of commutator spectral asymptotics and interpolation, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Operator-ADI Balanced Truncation Of Delay Differential Systems
authors: Timo Reis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a balanced truncation method for linear delay differential systems based on a finite-rank alternating-direction implicit (ADI) iteration for the associated operator Lyapunov equations. The method acts directly on the infinite-dimensional history-state realization and does not discretize the delay interval during Gramian approximation or balancing. The finite-rank reachability and observability factors are represented exactly in Takenaka--Malmquist coordinates, reducing the required computations to finite-dimensional linear algebra. These factors yield a finite-dimensional, delay-free reduced model. For real system data, the implementation remains in real arithmetic. Under suitable conditions on the ADI shifts and a gap in the Hankel singular values, we prove convergence in [MATH] to the reduced transfer function obtained by exact balanced truncation of the infinite-dimensional system. The construction extends to finitely many discrete delays. Numerical experiments validate the method against independent reference computations. The complete MATLAB implementation used in the experiments is provided as supplementary material.
tldr: A balanced truncation method is developed for linear delay differential systems using a finite-rank ADI iteration for operator Lyapunov equations, yielding finite-dimensional delay-free reduced models.
motivation: Model reduction for infinite-dimensional delay systems is challenging because direct discretization of the delay interval can be costly or inaccurate.
method: The approach uses a finite-rank alternating-direction implicit iteration on operator Lyapunov equations and represents reachability/observability factors in Takenaka-Malmquist coordinates, reducing computations to finite-dimensional linear algebra.
result: Under suitable ADI shifts and a Hankel singular value gap, the method converges in to the exact balanced truncation reduced transfer function; numerical experiments validate it and MATLAB code is provided.
conclusion: The method extends to finitely many discrete delays and provides an efficient, delay-free reduced-order modeling framework for delay differential systems.

title: Sppid: Saddle-Point Pid For Constrained Optimization
authors: Veronica Centorrino, Rawan Hoteit, Efe C. Balta, John Lygeros
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies constrained optimization problems through the lens of feedback control. Building on the interpretation of Lagrange multipliers as feedback controllers, we propose the : a unified proportional--integral--derivative (PID) framework for continuous-time saddle-point dynamics. The proposed dynamics employ PID control for equality constraints and anti-windup PI control for inequality constraints. We show that SPPID is equivalent to a preconditioned primal--dual gradient flow of the augmented Lagrangian. This equivalence reveals the distinct role of each feedback component: integral action enforces constraint satisfaction, proportional action induces the augmented Lagrangian structure, and derivative action modifies the geometry of the primal dynamics via a state-dependent Riemannian metric. For convex problems, we establish convergence to the KKT set together with conditions for global asymptotic stability. For equality-constrained problems, we establish local exponential convergence for nonlinear equality constraints under standard assumptions, and show that projected gradient flow emerges as the infinite derivative-gain limit. For strongly convex problems with affine equality or inequality constraints, we establish global exponential convergence by leveraging contraction theory. Finally, we provide various numerical examples to illustrate the utility of SPPID.
tldr: The paper proposes SPPID, a unified PID-based continuous-time saddle-point dynamics framework for constrained optimization, showing equivalence to preconditioned primal-dual gradient flow of the augmented Lagrangian.
motivation: Constrained optimization is studied through feedback control, interpreting Lagrange multipliers as controllers to unify and analyze saddle-point dynamics.
method: PID control is used for equality constraints and anti-windup PI for inequality constraints; the dynamics are recast as a preconditioned primal-dual gradient flow, with convergence analyzed via KKT conditions and contraction theory.
result: For convex problems, convergence to the KKT set and conditions for global asymptotic stability are established; local exponential convergence for nonlinear equality constraints and global exponential convergence for strongly convex problems with affine constraints are proved.
conclusion: SPPID provides a control-theoretic framework that clarifies the role of each PID component and connects to projected gradient flow as an infinite derivative-gain limit, with numerical examples illustrating its utility.

title: Solutions To The 'moment Property Implies Subnormality' And Injectivity Problems For Composition Operators On One-circuit Graphs
authors: Piotr Budzy\'nski, Zenon Jan Jab{\l}o\'nski, Il Bong Jung, Jan Stochel
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider composition operators in [MATH], where [MATH] is a discrete measure. Our main result shows that, for every integer [MATH], there exists a non-hyponormal composition operator that generates Stieltjes moment sequences and whose symbol induces a directed graph consisting of a circuit of length [MATH] and one infinite branch. In contrast, if the symbol induces a directed graph consisting of one loop and one infinite branch, then the generation of Stieltjes moment sequences does imply subnormality. These two results completely solve the ``moment property implies subnormality'' problem left open in [Adv. Math. 310 (2017), 484-556] for the entire family of one-branch directed graphs with a circuit of arbitrary length. Combining them with the examples in that paper shows that, for directed graphs consisting of one loop and a finite number of infinite branches, [MATH] is the smallest number of branches for which the moment property does not imply subnormality. Finally, we construct a noninjective composition operator that generates Stieltjes moment sequences and whose symbol induces a directed graph consisting of one loop, one infinite branch, and one leaf. This operator gives a negative answer to the injectivity problem posed in the aforementioned paper. Both constructions use the Krein and Friedrichs measures of an arbitrary normalized S-indeterminate Stieltjes moment sequence.
tldr: Solves the moment-property-implies-subnormality and injectivity problems for composition operators on one-circuit directed graphs using Krein and Friedrichs measures.
motivation: The paper addresses open problems from Adv. Math. 310 (2017) concerning when generation of Stieltjes moment sequences implies subnormality or injectivity for composition operators.
method: It constructs non-hyponormal composition operators whose symbols induce directed graphs with a circuit and infinite branches, using the Krein and Friedrichs measures of an arbitrary normalized S-indeterminate Stieltjes moment sequence.
result: For every integer n, a non-hyponormal operator generating Stieltjes moment sequences is constructed on a circuit of length n with one infinite branch, while the one-loop case implies subnormality; a noninjective example gives a negative answer to the injectivity problem.
conclusion: The results completely solve the moment-property-implies-subnormality problem for one-branch graphs with arbitrary circuit length and identify the minimal number of branches where the implication fails.

title: Explicity Defined Norms On $jt_*$ Spaces
authors: Pavlos Motakis Spiros A. Argyros
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Banach space [MATH], equipped with an explicit norm, whose properties resemble those of the predual [MATH] of the James Tree space. In particular, [MATH] admits a shrinking dyadic basis with the property that the sums of its elements over any segment are uniformly bounded. The space [MATH] is complementably [MATH]-saturated, and its dual [MATH] does not contain an isomorphic copy of [MATH]. Finally, the bidual [MATH] is also complementably [MATH]-saturated, and the quotient [MATH] is isometric to [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs a Banach space with an explicit norm whose properties mirror those of the predual of the James Tree space, including a shrinking dyadic basis and complementable saturation properties.
motivation: The James Tree space and its predual are classical objects in Banach space theory whose structure is subtle but typically described via implicit or non-explicit constructions; the authors aim to provide a concrete, explicitly normed counterpart.
method: The authors define a new Banach space with an explicit norm, verify it admits a shrinking dyadic basis with uniformly bounded segment sums, and analyze its saturation and duality properties.
result: The constructed space is complementably saturated, its dual contains no isomorphic copy of the relevant sequence space, its bidual is complementably saturated, and a certain quotient is isometric to a classical space.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit realization of James Tree space-like structure, contributing to the structural theory of Banach spaces, but it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Werracle: Sub-Cent Intra-Block Ai Reflex Oracles And Flash-Loan Circuit Breakers For Evm Smart Contracts
authors: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contemporary on-chain artificial intelligence (AI) encounters an intractable Von Neumann memory and latency wall. Storing static floating-point neural weight matrices inside Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) storage costs millions of gas, rendering direct on-chain inference impossible. While Zero-Knowledge Machine Learning (ZK-ML) offloads matrix tensor multiplications to off-chain provers, it introduces fatal constraints: 10 to 300 seconds of SNARK proving latency and 250,000 to 500,000 gas per proof verification. Because decentralized finance (DeFi) exploits - such as uncollateralized flash-loan attacks, predatory sandwich MEV, and toxic loss-versus-rebalancing (LVR) flow - occur atomically inside a single block, ZK-ML oracles cannot react in time. Here, we present Werracle, a production-grade, zero-storage on-chain AI decision oracle fitting inside a single 32-byte EVM storage slot (bytes32). Leveraging foundational procedural Mandelbrot escape dynamics (z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c) established by Dagli et al. (arXiv:2609.25498), Werracle derives continuous non-linear decision hyperplanes from a 24-byte coordinate triplet Theta = (c_x, c_y, zoom). Implemented in pure Solidity bytecode using fixed-point Q16.16 arithmetic (WerrMath.sol), Werracle evaluates a 16-point Pareto micro-grid in only 21,438 gas (under 0.0005 USD on Layer-2 rollups like Base and Arbitrum) with sub-millisecond execution latency. We demonstrate real-world DeFi efficacy via WerracleFeeHook.sol, a Uniswap v4 dynamic swap fee governor that measures orderbook turbulence on-the-fly and atomically adjusts liquidity provider fees between 0.05% and 0.50%. The protocol is formally verified against a 1,000-test cryptographically sealed deterministic verification suite (100.0% pass rate) with telemetry permanently disabled, operating live on a dedicated EVM devnet sandbox (Chain ID 4242).
tldr: Werracle proposes a zero-storage on-chain AI oracle for EVM smart contracts that uses Mandelbrot escape dynamics and fixed-point arithmetic to enable sub-cent intra-block DeFi risk decisions.
motivation: Contemporary on-chain AI faces prohibitive storage costs and ZK-ML proving latency, making atomic DeFi attack mitigation infeasible.
method: It encodes decision hyperplanes in a 24-byte coordinate triplet and evaluates a 16-point Pareto micro-grid in pure Solidity with Q16.16 fixed-point arithmetic, plus a Uniswap v4 dynamic fee hook.
result: The oracle evaluates in 21,438 gas with sub-millisecond latency, adjusts liquidity provider fees between 0.05% and 0.50%, and passes a 1,000-test deterministic verification suite on a devnet.
conclusion: The work delivers a production-grade, low-cost EVM-native AI oracle for block-level DeFi protection, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory or the listed research directions.

title: Input-Layer Starvation: Why Per-Layer Pruning Breaks IoT Intrusion Detectors
authors: Md Anas Biswas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrusion detectors for small Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices are usually compressed by pruning and judged by overall accuracy. We show that this hides a severe class-level failure, find its cause, and give low-overhead prevention and repair. On CICIoT2023, a two-layer convolutional detector pruned with uniform layer-wise magnitude pruning at 80% sparsity loses 16 points of accuracy but half of its macro-F1, the mean per-class F1 (0.542 to 0.271 over five independently trained models); 17 of 34 classes are materially damaged. Remaining weight count does not explain it: a perceptron and a transformer pruned to the same or fewer weights lose at most 0.096. The first layer does. It has 192 weights; uniform pruning leaves 38, 46% of its 64 filters lose every input weight, and fine-tuning under that starvation leaves the running means of the first normalisation layer displaced by up to 0.8 standard deviations in a few surviving channels, on which the deployed model collapses. Protecting those 192 weights, or pruning globally at the same sparsity, prevents the collapse (loss 0.013); recomputing the normalisation statistics on unlabelled training data, with no weight changed, repairs it (loss 0.039) and returns the false-alert rate to 33% (dense 29%). Damage shows a strong increasing dose-response in first-layer sparsity, starving a perceptron's input layer reproduces the collapse, and the pattern holds on TON_IoT. The failure is misattribution and false alerts, not silent evasion: on validation-selected blind spots, uniformly pruned detectors misattribute 72% of the traffic, against 50% with the first layer protected and 47% for the dense model.
tldr: Per-layer magnitude pruning in small IoT intrusion detectors can starve the input layer, causing severe class-level performance collapse that is hidden by overall accuracy.
motivation: Pruned IoT intrusion detectors are usually evaluated by overall accuracy, which may mask severe per-class failures and misleading false-alert behavior.
method: The paper analyzes a two-layer CNN on CICIoT2023 and TON_IoT under uniform layer-wise magnitude pruning, comparing damaged first-layer filters, global pruning, and normalization-statistics repair on unlabeled data.
result: At 80% sparsity, uniform pruning halves macro-F1 from 0.542 to 0.271 while accuracy drops only 16 points; protecting the 192 first-layer weights or pruning globally prevents collapse, and recomputing normalization statistics repairs it without changing weights.
conclusion: The failure is caused by first-layer starvation and manifests as misattribution and false alerts rather than silent evasion, so layer-aware or global pruning and normalization recalibration are needed for reliable IoT intrusion detection.

title: JevAdvBench: A Benchmark And Black-Box Attacks For Reinforcement Learning For Calibrated Decisions Models
authors: Jianyi Hu, Hangtao Zhang, Yi Liu, Yeqi Zeng, Li Zeng, Xianlong Wang, Rui Wang, Leo Yu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Models trained with reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions (RLCD), such as Jev, answer a typed question about an input, the state, with a probability, a choice, or a score, and software acts on the answer without a person reading it. Their robustness has not been measured: adversarial benchmarks score what a model generates or executes, whereas a typed model generates nothing and returns a well-formed answer even when manipulated. Measurement is also hard, because identical requests can return different answers, most available labels come from the model itself, and the API preprocesses each request out of view. Our key idea is to score each attacked decision against the model's own clean decision rather than against labels, and to read it against the change caused by an identical re-run. Building on this, we introduce JevAdvBench, to our knowledge the first adversarial benchmark for RLCD models, with 812 typed questions over 66 scenarios, and a black-box attack suite of 9,744 single-edit variants that each edit one part of a request, with billed input tokens confirming that the edit reached the model. On jev-1.13.0, rewording stays within 1.2 percentage points of the re-run baseline, and fields outside the schema never reach the model. In contrast, one unverified opinion appended to the state flips 12.1% of decisions, statistically tied with the strongest injected command (10.1%), and pushes 38% of confident answers below the 0.8 confidence threshold that routes them to human review. Applications built on RLCD models should therefore treat the state as untrusted, argued input. Project website: [URL].
tldr: The paper introduces JevAdvBench, the first adversarial benchmark for reinforcement-learning-calibrated decision models, and a black-box attack suite that reveals single-edit vulnerabilities in typed decision outputs.
motivation: Models trained with reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions return typed answers that software may act on without human review, but their adversarial robustness has not been measured before.
method: The authors build a benchmark of 812 typed questions across 66 scenarios and a suite of 9,744 single-edit attack variants, scoring each attacked decision against the model's own clean decision and against identical re-run variation.
result: On jev-1.13.0, rewording stays within 1.2 percentage points of the baseline and schema-external fields never reach the model, while one unverified opinion appended to the state flips 12.1% of decisions and pushes 38% of confident answers below the 0.8 confidence threshold.
conclusion: Applications built on RLCD models should treat the state as untrusted, argued input, since even simple appended opinions can substantially alter calibrated decisions and trigger human review.

title: The Existence Of Polyhedral Invariants Is Undecidable For Linear Systems
authors: David Monniaux
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence of polyhedral inductive invariants suitable for proving that a given control location is unreachable is undecidable for programs using only linear arithmetic over Z or Q, by reduction from 2-counter machines.
tldr: The existence of polyhedral inductive invariants for proving unreachability in linear-arithmetic programs is shown undecidable via a reduction from 2-counter machines.
motivation: Polyhedral invariants are a standard tool in program verification, and understanding the limits of automatically finding them is important for static analysis.
method: The paper reduces the halting problem for 2-counter machines to the existence of a polyhedral inductive invariant sufficient to prove a control location unreachable, for programs over integers or rationals with linear arithmetic.
result: It proves that deciding whether such a polyhedral invariant exists is undecidable for linear systems over Z or Q.
conclusion: The existence of polyhedral inductive invariants is undecidable, implying fundamental limitations for automated invariant generation in linear-arithmetic program verification.

title: Context-Aware Functional Modeling For Android Third-Party Library Detection
authors: Dihao Fan, Jian Zhang, Yasai Shi, Chuan Luo, Xudong Liu, Yang Liu, Chunming Hu, Xu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-party libraries (TPLs) are widely used in Android apps, but their reuse can introduce security risks and interfere with downstream program analyses. Existing Android TPL detection approaches face two key limitations: their hand-crafted features are fragile under aggressive code transformations, and their whole-library matching strategies are ineffective when apps retain only part of a TPL. In this paper, we propose LibFan, a learning-based Android TPL detection approach based on context-aware functional modeling. It realizes this modeling through two complementary components: context-aware contrastive learning at the method level and functional partitioning at the library level. At the method level, it learns semantic representations through contrastive training while incorporating outgoing call relationships and class-level context, improving robustness to obfuscation, shrinking, and optimization. At the library level, it partitions each TPL into functionally coherent units and determines library presence using the best-matching partition, thereby accommodating partial library reuse. To evaluate LibFan, we construct a new benchmark comprising 200 apps and 46 vulnerable TPLs, with each app compiled under four transformation configurations. Under the most challenging R8 full mode, LibFan achieves F1 scores of 81.3% at the library level and 47.6% at the version level, representing relative improvements of 64.9% and 35.6% over the state of the art, respectively.
tldr: LibFan is a learning-based approach for detecting third-party libraries in Android apps using context-aware functional modeling.
motivation: Third-party library reuse in Android apps introduces security risks and complicates program analysis, but existing detection methods struggle with code transformations and partial library reuse.
method: LibFan combines method-level context-aware contrastive learning with library-level functional partitioning to improve robustness and accommodate partial matches.
result: On a new benchmark of 200 apps and 46 vulnerable TPLs, LibFan achieves F1 scores of 81.3% at the library level and 47.6% at the version level under R8 full mode, improving over state of the art by 64.9% and 35.6%.
conclusion: Context-aware functional modeling significantly enhances Android third-party library detection under aggressive code transformations and partial reuse scenarios.

title: Verifiable Randomness For Blockchain-Based Lottery Systems
authors: Gon\c{c}alo Ferreira, Andr\'e Z\'uquete, Paulo Bartolomeu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As lotteries and other high-stakes decentralized applications increasingly depend on unpredictable randomness for their operations, the lack of a secure and transparent on-chain random number generator that is verifiable by all participants remains a critical open problem. Various approaches to blockchain-based random number generation have emerged over the years, each with their own strengths and limitations, and have consistently been superseded as blockchain technology evolved. This paper surveys existing approaches to on-chain randomness and proposes a new platform that builds upon the well-known commit-and-reveal scheme while directly addressing its principal vulnerability, the last revealer attack, in which the final participant can withhold their reveal in order to bias or abort the output upon seeing an unfavorable result. We further compare this solution with prior approaches and evaluate its entropy properties. The proposed architecture combines a web-based front-end with a Solidity smart contract deployed on the Polygon 2.0 blockchain. Implemented and tested on the Amoy testnet, the prototype is low-cost and simple to deploy, providing a practical, accessible proof-of-concept for verifiable on-chain randomness.
tldr: This paper surveys blockchain-based randomness generation and proposes a commit-and-reveal lottery platform on Polygon 2.0 that mitigates the last-revealer attack.
motivation: Decentralized lotteries and high-stakes applications require unpredictable, verifiable on-chain randomness, yet existing schemes suffer from attacks such as the last-revealer bias.
method: The authors analyze prior on-chain randomness approaches and design a new commit-and-reveal architecture combining a web front-end with a Solidity smart contract, implemented and tested on the Amoy testnet.
result: The prototype is low-cost and simple to deploy, and the paper evaluates its entropy properties while comparing it to existing methods.
conclusion: The proposed platform provides a practical proof-of-concept for verifiable on-chain randomness, though it remains classical and does not address quantum information or thermodynamic concerns.

title: Toward Verifiably Private Learning From Federated Data
authors: Katharine Daly, Yu Xiao, Zachary Garrett, Brett Mclarnon, Jianpeng Hou, Arun Ganesh, Yanxiang Zhang, Noriyuki Takahashi, Haicheng Sun, Yuanbo Zhang, Timon van Overveldt, Daniel Ramage
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) allows devices with private data to collaborate in training a shared model. We present a next-generation FL system based on Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) that addresses operational challenges associated with earlier systems and provides externally verifiable central Differential Privacy (DP) guarantees for the first time while offering a better privacy-utility tradeoff. In our system, devices upload data encrypted with keys managed by a TEE-hosted Key Management Service (KMS). The uploaded data is cryptographically tied to a policy limiting the set of Python programs that may later process the data in server-side TEEs. External parties may inspect public transparency logs to observe the set of workloads allowed by these policies. Our experimental results show that the new system improves device coverage and favorably shifts privacy-utility curves by enabling collected data to be integrated into the server-side workload at a schedule that optimizes DP guarantees and is unaffected by device availability. Our new system has been productionized, enabling models for the Android Keyboard (Gboard) to be trained faster and achieve better accuracy under smaller, now externally verifiable privacy budgets in comparison to models trained using the prior system.
tldr: The paper presents a productionized federated learning system using trusted execution environments and differential privacy to provide externally verifiable privacy guarantees with improved privacy-utility tradeoffs.
motivation: Federated learning enables collaborative model training on private data, but existing systems face operational challenges and lack externally verifiable central differential privacy guarantees.
method: The system uses TEE-managed key encryption for uploaded device data, cryptographically ties data to policies limiting server-side Python workloads, exposes transparency logs for external verification, and schedules data integration to optimize differential privacy guarantees.
result: Experimental results show improved device coverage, better privacy-utility curves unaffected by device availability, and production deployment for Gboard training with faster and more accurate models under smaller verifiable privacy budgets.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical, verifiably private federated learning system that advances industrial privacy-preserving machine learning, though it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fast And Secure Simultaneous Authentication Of Equals For Wpa3
authors: Jo\~ao Ferreira, Andr\'e Z\'uquete, H\'elder Gomes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) protocol, introduced in WPA3, provides robust protection against offline dictionary attacks against a network Pre-Shared Key (PSK) and also protection of session keys from other people knowing that PSK. However, its high computational cost for the Password Element (PE) derivation makes Access Points (APs) vulnerable to CPU exhaustion Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. This paper proposes a resilient architectural modification to SAE. First, we introduce an asymmetric resource cost model that offloads the iterative discovery of cryptographic elements to the client, allowing the AP to maintain a fixed computational load during the handshake. To further mitigate brute-force attempts, we implement a mechanism based on a slow-path key derivation (with variable cost key derivation functions, such as PBKDF2 or Argon2), incorporating a deliberate processing delay on the supplicant. Finally, we introduce a ticket-based mechanism to facilitate efficient re-authentication for known devices, bypassing expensive exchanges while preserving system availability under adversarial conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that this architecture significantly mitigates DoS risks without compromising legitimate network access.
tldr: The paper proposes an architectural modification to WPA3's Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) protocol to mitigate CPU exhaustion DoS attacks by offloading computational cost to clients and introducing slow-path key derivation and ticket-based re-authentication.
motivation: SAE's high computational cost for Password Element derivation makes Access Points vulnerable to CPU exhaustion Denial-of-Service attacks.
method: The authors introduce an asymmetric resource cost model that shifts iterative discovery to the client, implement a slow-path key derivation with variable cost functions (e.g., PBKDF2, Argon2) to add deliberate delay, and use a ticket-based mechanism for efficient re-authentication.
result: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture significantly mitigates DoS risks while preserving legitimate network access and system availability under adversarial conditions.
conclusion: The modified SAE protocol enhances resilience against DoS attacks without compromising authentication security or performance for legitimate users.

title: FragToken: Amplifying Llm Inference Costs Through Noncanonical Token Generation
authors: Zihan Wang, Rui Zhang, Xinyuan Qian, Qingchuan Zhao, Hongwei Li, Guowen Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language model (LLM) inference becomes increasingly expensive, resource-consumption attacks pose a growing threat to model providers. Existing attacks typically amplify cost by inducing abnormally long or repetitive outputs on attacker-controlled or triggered requests, making them easier to detect and limiting their deployment-wide impact when benign traffic dominates. In this work, we uncover a previously overlooked token-level attack surface arising from the many-to-one mapping from token sequences to decoded text. Although standard LLMs predominantly generate the canonical token sequences induced by their tokenizers, the same text can also be represented by substantially longer non-canonical sequences. This representational flexibility exposes a new avenue for resource-consumption attacks: an attacker can train the model to favor such sequences, systematically increasing the number of autoregressive decoding steps without a proportional increase in visible response length. However, we empirically find that directly maximizing token fragmentation substantially degrades model utility, producing conspicuous answer-quality failures that undermine attack stealthiness. To address this challenge, we propose FragToken, a training-time framework that combines source-model self-distillation, capacity-aware filtering and budgeting, and BPE-Aligned Merging to induce fragmented generation under ordinary prompts while largely preserving model utility. We evaluate FragToken on four LLMs across three benchmarks. Across the four models, FragToken achieves a three-benchmark average token inflation ratio (TIR) ranging from 1.99 to 2.46, while causing only minor degradation in model utility. Our work reveals a covert LLM supply-chain threat that increases inference cost without requiring large volumes of attack requests while largely preserving utility.
tldr: The paper introduces FragToken, a training-time framework that induces LLMs to generate noncanonical token sequences to amplify inference costs with minimal visible output growth.
motivation: LLM inference is expensive, and existing resource-consumption attacks are easily detected because they produce abnormally long or repetitive outputs; a stealthier token-level attack surface is needed.
method: FragToken combines source-model self-distillation, capacity-aware filtering and budgeting, and BPE-Aligned Merging to train models to favor fragmented token sequences under ordinary prompts while preserving utility.
result: Across four LLMs and three benchmarks, FragToken achieves average token inflation ratios of 1.99 to 2.46 with only minor degradation in model utility.
conclusion: The work exposes a covert LLM supply-chain threat that increases inference cost without requiring large volumes of attack requests and while largely preserving utility.

title: A Nonoverlapping Spectral Additive Schwarz Method For Interior Penalty Discontinuous Galerkin Discretizations Of Anisotropic Elliptic Problems
authors: Maurice S. Fabien, Sijing Liu, Marcus Sarkis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design and analyze a nonoverlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner for interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of anisotropic elliptic problems. The preconditioned method coupled with a Krylov subspace iteration is shown to be independent of the highly discontinuous (and anisotropic) jump coefficients as well as the subdomain size. To increase efficacy, various auxiliary spaces are considered to reduce the size of the coarse grid operator. We demonstrate how to modify the additive Schwarz preconditioner such that it is applicable to the nonsymmetric IPDG schemes. Several numerical experiments verify the theory and validate the robustness of the preconditioner.
tldr: This paper designs and analyzes a nonoverlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner for interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of anisotropic elliptic problems.
motivation: Anisotropic elliptic problems with highly discontinuous jump coefficients are challenging to solve efficiently, requiring preconditioners whose convergence is robust to coefficient variation and mesh/subdomain size.
method: The authors construct a nonoverlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner coupled with Krylov subspace iteration, introduce auxiliary spaces to reduce the coarse grid operator size, and extend the approach to nonsymmetric IPDG schemes.
result: The preconditioned method is proven to be independent of the anisotropic jump coefficients and subdomain size, and numerical experiments verify the theory and confirm robustness.
conclusion: The proposed preconditioner provides a theoretically sound and numerically validated solver for anisotropic elliptic problems discretized via IPDG, though it lies entirely within numerical analysis and scientific computing.

title: Sparsely Connected Rank-inspired Neural Network
authors: Yunqing Huang, Wu Su, Nianyu Yi, Peimeng Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a Sparsely Connected Rank-Inspired Neural Network (SCRINN) for function approximation and the numerical solution of partial differential equations (PDEs). By introducing a structured sparse connectivity architecture and an orthogonality- and normalization-guided loss function, SCRINN constructs an approximately orthonormal neural basis while promoting progressive rank growth of its evaluation matrix and reducing the number of trainable parameters. A two-stage framework is developed, in which an approximately orthonormal neural basis is first constructed, and the output weights are subsequently determined using least-squares methods. Numerical experiments on function approximation and a variety of steady-state, time-dependent, and nonlinear PDEs demonstrate that SCRINN consistently achieves high approximation accuracy with substantially lower training costs. The code is publicly available on GitHub.
tldr: The paper introduces SCRINN, a sparsely connected, rank-inspired neural network architecture for function approximation and numerical solution of PDEs.
motivation: Standard neural network solvers for PDEs require large numbers of trainable parameters and high training costs, and lack structured bases that promote good conditioning and expressivity.
method: A structured sparse connectivity architecture combined with an orthogonality- and normalization-guided loss builds an approximately orthonormal neural basis with progressive rank growth; a two-stage scheme first constructs the basis and then determines output weights via least-squares.
result: Numerical experiments on function approximation and steady-state, time-dependent, and nonlinear PDEs show consistently high accuracy with substantially reduced training cost and fewer trainable parameters.
conclusion: SCRINN offers an efficient, low-parameter alternative for scientific machine learning and PDE solvers, though it has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Deep-Learning Solvers And Surrogates For Infinity And p-Laplace Problems
authors: Tak Shing Au Yeung, Ka Chun Cheung, Hannah Potgieter, Steven J. Ruuth, Simon See
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the use of neural network solvers for infinity and [MATH]-Laplace problems, which are fundamental in nonlinear analysis and have practical applications. Our approach employs Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) to address computational challenges associated with large [MATH] values, ranging from [MATH] to [MATH], on various 2D and 3D domains. Our method offers advantages over traditional physics-based solvers, especially in three dimensions where mesh-based solvers become very costly for these problems. We also establish conditional convergence results for PINN approximations of both problems and a universal approximation result for DeepONet on the parametric [MATH]-Poisson problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of these neural network solvers through numerical experiments and compare their performance with conventional methods.
tldr: The paper develops Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Deep Operator Networks as mesh-free solvers and surrogates for infinity-Laplace and p-Laplace nonlinear PDE problems in 2D and 3D.
motivation: Classical mesh-based numerical solvers become prohibitively expensive for infinity- and p-Laplace problems, especially in three dimensions and for large p values, motivating learning-based alternatives.
method: The authors train PINNs and DeepONets on 2D/3D domains across a wide range of p values, and prove conditional convergence results for PINN approximations plus a universal approximation theorem for DeepONet on the parametric p-Poisson problem.
result: Numerical experiments show the neural solvers are effective and competitive or advantageous relative to conventional physics-based solvers, particularly in 3D where meshing is costly.
conclusion: Neural network solvers and operator surrogates offer a practical, theoretically supported route for high-dimensional nonlinear PDE problems, though the work is purely numerical-analysis focused and unrelated to quantum information.

title: A Vanishing-viscosity Minimizing Movement Fourier Spectral Method For Scalar Conservation Laws
authors: Lun Ji, Buyang Li, Fangyan Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a vanishing-viscosity minimizing movement (VVMM) Fourier spectral method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws under periodic boundary conditions. The method is a fully discrete space--time residual-minimizing scheme, Fourier spectral in space and polynomial in time, stabilized by vanishing viscosity and heat-kernel postprocessing. A basic analytical difficulty in Fourier discretizations of nonlinear conservation laws is the interaction between Fourier projection and the nonlinear flux; the resulting projection residual contains unresolved high-frequency components. VVMM addresses this issue by selecting, on each time slab, the numerical solution that minimizes {a penalized cut-off viscous conservation laws residual} and then applies heat-kernel postprocessing to damp unresolved modes. We prove a fully discrete [MATH] error estimate, in any fixed space dimension, that separates the vanishing-viscosity error, the temporal interpolation error, and the spatial Fourier truncation error. {Under exact minimization of the penalized cut-off residual and suitable parameter coupling,} the estimate yields, for each fixed [MATH], an [MATH] convergence rate [MATH], with a constant depending on [MATH]. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions illustrate stable shock capturing without visible Gibbs oscillations and convergence behavior consistent with the theory.
tldr: The paper introduces a vanishing-viscosity minimizing movement Fourier spectral method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws with provable fully discrete error estimates and stable shock capture.
motivation: Fourier spectral discretizations of nonlinear conservation laws suffer from projection residuals containing unresolved high-frequency components, which complicates accurate shock capturing under periodic boundary conditions.
method: The authors propose a fully discrete space–time residual-minimizing scheme that is Fourier spectral in space and polynomial in time, stabilized by vanishing viscosity and heat-kernel postprocessing that damps unresolved modes on each time slab.
result: They prove a fully discrete error estimate in any fixed space dimension that separates vanishing-viscosity, temporal interpolation, and Fourier truncation errors, yielding a convergence rate with constants depending on the dimension; 1D and 2D experiments show stable shock capturing without visible Gibbs oscillations.
conclusion: The VVMM Fourier spectral method provides a theoretically grounded and numerically stable approach for solving scalar conservation laws, though it lies entirely within numerical analysis and PDE theory.

title: Tight Stochastic Condition-Number Dependence In Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
authors: Qihao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study whether the linear condition-number dependence in the stochastic complexity of SAPD+ is necessary for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization. For jointly [MATH]-smooth objectives with dual strong-concavity parameter [MATH], we prove a lower bound that matches the SAPD+ upper bound under the same Moreau-envelope stationarity criterion and the same primal-dual initialization gap. Specifically, when [MATH], the worst-case complexity of zero-respecting algorithms is [MATH] in the stated accuracy regime, where [MATH], [MATH] bounds the initial primal-dual gap, and [MATH] bounds the variance of a general unbiased first-order oracle. The lower bound is realized on a smooth problem class with a bounded dual box. Our construction routes each link of a nonconvex zero-chain through a dual gradient of magnitude proportional to [MATH], while an undiscovered primal coordinate prevents stationarity. It also yields the primal-gradient lower bound [MATH] after combination with the known deterministic bound, where [MATH] bounds the initial primal function gap.
tldr: The paper establishes a tight lower bound on the stochastic complexity of nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization, matching the SAPD+ upper bound and showing that linear condition-number dependence is necessary.
motivation: The authors investigate whether the linear condition-number dependence observed in stochastic algorithms for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization is fundamental or an artifact of existing methods.
method: They prove a worst-case lower bound for zero-respecting algorithms using a smooth problem class with a bounded dual box, routing each nonconvex zero-chain link through a dual gradient scaled by the condition number.
result: Under the stated accuracy regime, the worst-case complexity is characterized by the condition number, initial primal-dual gap, and oracle variance, matching the SAPD+ upper bound and yielding a primal-gradient lower bound after combination with deterministic results.
conclusion: The linear condition-number dependence in the stochastic complexity of SAPD+ for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization is unavoidable for zero-respecting algorithms under the Moreau-envelope stationarity criterion.

title: Retraction-Based Gradient Projection Algorithms On Manifolds
authors: Hao Wu Conglong Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a framework for retraction-based convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds, which includes a notion of retraction-specific convex sets and retraction-based gradient projection algorithms. The standard theory of gradient projection algorithms generalizes easily to this framework. Within this framework, we establish convergence results for retraction-based gradient projection algorithms with various stepsize rules. As an application, we use our framework to study the weighted low-rank approximation. We also provide numerical validation of our convergence results on the image completion task.
tldr: The paper develops a framework for retraction-based convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds, including retraction-specific convex sets and gradient projection algorithms with convergence guarantees.
motivation: Gradient projection methods are well understood in Euclidean spaces, but extending them to Riemannian manifolds requires a consistent notion of convexity compatible with the chosen retraction.
method: The authors define retraction-based convex sets and retraction-based gradient projection algorithms, then prove convergence under various stepsize rules, applying the framework to weighted low-rank approximation.
result: Convergence results are established for the proposed algorithms under multiple stepsize schemes, and numerical experiments on image completion validate the theoretical findings.
conclusion: The framework generalizes classical gradient projection theory to manifolds and offers a practical tool for matrix problems such as weighted low-rank approximation.

title: A Bregman Inertial Iteratively Regularized Extragradient Method For Bilevel Variational Inequality Problems
authors: Kangming Chen, Atsushi Hori, Ellen H. Fukuda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider bilevel variational inequality problems, where the feasible set is the solution set of another variational inequality. We propose a Bregman inertial regularized extragradient method for solving these problems. By performing the inertial extrapolation in the dual space, the proposed method aligns the inertial step with the structure of the Bregman three-point identity. We also derive explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the generalized gap function. More precisely, using diminishing regularization, we establish convergence rates of [MATH] for the optimality gap and [MATH] for the feasibility gap with [MATH]. For constant regularization parameter [MATH], we establish an [MATH] rate for the optimality gap and an [MATH] bound for the feasibility gap. Furthermore, numerical experiments on traffic networks and multi-portfolio Nash equilibrium problems demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed framework.
tldr: The paper proposes a Bregman inertial iteratively regularized extragradient method for solving bilevel variational inequality problems, with non-asymptotic convergence rates and numerical validation.
motivation: Bilevel variational inequality problems, where the feasible set is itself the solution set of another variational inequality, arise in applications such as traffic networks and Nash equilibrium computation but are computationally challenging.
method: The authors perform inertial extrapolation in the dual space to align with the Bregman three-point identity, combining Bregman regularization with an extragradient scheme under both diminishing and constant regularization parameters.
result: They derive explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the generalized gap function, obtaining sublinear convergence rates for the optimality gap and feasibility gap, and demonstrate effectiveness on traffic network and multi-portfolio Nash equilibrium problems.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a principled inertial Bregman extragradient approach with provable convergence guarantees for bilevel variational inequalities, supported by numerical experiments.

title: Long-time And Large-population Limits Of Displacement Monotone Linear-quadratic Nash Systems
authors: Davide Francesco Redaelli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For linear-quadratic [MATH]-dimensional Nash systems with mean-field-like scaling and strongly displacement monotone data, we prove uniform-in-time a priori derivative estimates exhibiting the expected scaling as [MATH] in order to pass the system to the limit. As a consequence, in a heterogeneous (i.e., non-symmetric) mean-field setting, we obtain both uniform-in-time convergence of the Nash system on any arbitrarily long horizon [MATH] (as [MATH]), and convergence of both the [MATH]-dimensional Nash system and the corresponding master equation to their respective ergodic counterparts (as [MATH]).
tldr: The paper establishes uniform-in-time a priori derivative estimates for strongly displacement monotone linear-quadratic mean-field Nash systems, deriving long-horizon and large-population convergence to ergodic limits.
motivation: Mean-field Nash systems and their master equations are central objects in stochastic control and mean-field game theory, but passing them to long-time and large-population limits requires uniform-in-time regularity estimates that were previously lacking.
method: The author proves uniform-in-time a priori estimates on derivatives exhibiting the expected scaling in the population dimension N for linear-quadratic systems with strongly displacement monotone data, then passes to the limit in both horizon and population size.
result: The paper obtains uniform-in-time convergence of the N-dimensional Nash system over arbitrarily long horizons and convergence of both the Nash system and its master equation to their ergodic counterparts.
conclusion: Displacement monotonicity provides sufficient structure to control long-time behavior in heterogeneous mean-field settings, yielding ergodic limits for Nash systems and master equations.

title: Energy-minimizing Domain Decomposition
authors: Muhammad Hassan, Benjamin Stamm, Lambert Theisen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.31182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel domain decomposition framework based on energy minimization, applicable to a wide class of linear and nonlinear partial differential equations. This energy-minimizing domain decomposition (EMDD) method addresses problems whose solutions are minimizers of an energy functional, either unconstrained or constrained to a manifold, and thus covers source and eigenvalue problems in a single formulation. Besides introducing the general framework, we derive the algorithmic realization of the method for four classes of model problems, namely linear and nonlinear source and eigenvalue problems, and derive the computational complexity of the method. Numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness and efficiency of the method across all four model problems and show that it compares favourably against existing model-specific domain decomposition methods.
tldr: The paper introduces an energy-minimizing domain decomposition (EMDD) framework for solving linear and nonlinear PDEs whose solutions minimize energy functionals, including both source and eigenvalue problems.
motivation: Existing domain decomposition methods tend to be tailored to specific problem classes, so a unified formulation covering source and eigenvalue problems, both linear and nonlinear, is desirable.
method: The authors formulate domain decomposition as an energy minimization over (possibly manifold-constrained) energy functionals, derive algorithmic realizations for four model problem classes, and analyze computational complexity.
result: Numerical experiments across linear/nonlinear source and eigenvalue problems show robustness, efficiency, and favorable comparison against model-specific domain decomposition methods.
conclusion: EMDD provides a general, unified, and computationally efficient framework for a broad class of PDE problems, though it lies entirely within numerical analysis rather than quantum information science.

title: Too Late To Slash: Coordinating A Risk-Free Equivocation Attack
authors: Chen-Da Liu-Zhang Hao Chung
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Slashing is commonly argued to secure proof-of-stake blockchains by confiscating the stake of misbehaving validators. The usual justification is that, without slashing, validators can solicit an equivocation attack by signing conflicting blocks: if enough others join, the attack succeeds; otherwise, the attempt incurs no loss. Slashing is intended to make such attempts costly and thereby guarantee the security of applications whose economic value is comparable to the bonded stake. This rationale, however, rests on heuristic arguments rather than a formal game-theoretic guarantee. We challenge this rationale by constructing a risk-free coordination protocol for rational validators under algorithmic slashing. We show that the prescribed strategy profile, in which rational validators solicit other validators to equivocate, constitutes an ex post Nash equilibrium, even when validators do not know in advance how many others will participate. The equilibrium holds for any gain [MATH] from successful equivocation, however small relative to the bonded stake. Thus, slashing alone does not guarantee economic security proportional to the value of bonded stake. Our results expose a fundamental limitation of algorithmic slashing. Whereas conventional collateral arrangements in many real-world scenarios can rely on external enforcement, for example through courts, algorithmic slashing depends on the same consensus process that the attackers control. These findings call for a formal analysis of slashing's security, rather than overly simplistic arguments drawn from financial systems with independent enforcement.
tldr: The paper constructs a risk-free coordination protocol for rational validators in proof-of-stake blockchains, showing that algorithmic slashing cannot prevent equivocation attacks and thus fails to guarantee economic security.
motivation: Slashing is widely assumed to deter equivocation by making attacks costly, but this justification rests on heuristic arguments rather than a formal game-theoretic foundation. The authors aim to test whether slashing alone actually guarantees security proportional to bonded stake.
method: The authors construct an explicit coordination strategy profile among rational validators under algorithmic slashing and analyze it using game-theoretic equilibrium concepts, specifically showing it forms an ex post Nash equilibrium even under uncertainty about others' participation.
result: The prescribed strategy—validators soliciting others to equivocate—constitutes an ex post Nash equilibrium, and this holds for any gain from successful equivocation, however small relative to the bonded stake, revealing that slashing alone does not ensure economic security.
conclusion: Algorithmic slashing faces a fundamental limitation because it relies on the same consensus process attackers may control, unlike collateral arrangements backed by external enforcement, motivating a more formal analysis of slashing-based security.

title: Proportional Representation In Temporal Voting With Ranked Preferences
authors: Noam Hazon, Leora Schmerler, Nicholas Teh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.30555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study proportional representation in temporal voting, where one candidate is selected in each round. While prior work has focused on approval ballots, we consider ranked preferences, which may change over time. A natural approach treats each voter's top candidates as approved, but the right cutoff may differ across voters and rounds. We therefore require proportionality to hold for every admissible choice of cutoffs, whether fixed and common, common but varying across rounds, or set individually for each voter in each round. Combining these interpretations with temporal versions of justified representation (JR), proportional JR (PJR), extended JR (EJR), and proportionality for solid coalitions (PSC) gives us a hierarchy of axioms. We ask which of these axioms can be guaranteed, and with how much knowledge of the future. Unlike with approval ballots, no version of EJR can be guaranteed, and for the other axioms, flexibility in the cutoffs comes at a price. With a fixed common cutoff, JR, PJR, and PSC can be guaranteed, but only by rules that see all preferences in advance.
